selected_leaf: Derive the minimal verifier observation contract for concurrent or eventually-consistent targets so an already ambiguous Stage T effect can be classified as COMMITTED, CONFLICT, or UNKNOWN without any second target mutation call.

bounded_leaf_result.tested_scope: Abstract recurring-Chat Stage T protocols continuing from durable VERIFY_PENDING for one logical_effect_id and intended tuple (T,w,d). The verifier is read-only and must tolerate concurrent unrelated writes and eventual visibility. No concrete target API, provider availability, cross-target guarantee, or richer-mode capability is claimed.

minimal_observation_contract.authoritative_target_identity: Every observation names the exact target object or namespace and is target-authoritative rather than reconstructed solely from client-local acknowledgement or checkpoint state.
minimal_observation_contract.monotone_version_witness: Every decisive observation carries a target version, event sequence, snapshot epoch, or equivalent monotone witness V that lets the verifier distinguish a newer observation from an older one and bind the observed value to a specific target state frontier.
minimal_observation_contract.freshness_or_coverage_witness: For negative evidence, V alone is insufficient. The read surface must also expose a coverage/finality fact H establishing which target admissions, events, or object versions are guaranteed to be reflected by this observation. If H cannot be related to the effect's relevant submission/admission horizon, absence remains UNKNOWN.
minimal_observation_contract.effect_correlation_uniqueness: Positive evidence must bind uniquely to logical_effect_id, or to a target-side key/request digest/effect fingerprint that is injective within the tested namespace. Equality of final object value without unique correlation is not enough because a concurrent unrelated write may coincidentally produce the same value.
minimal_observation_contract.request_digest_binding: When a target-side idempotency or effect record is used, the record must bind the stable key to the intended request digest d and outcome. Same key plus incompatible digest is decisive conflict evidence; a mutable or client-authored mapping is not authoritative.
minimal_observation_contract.concurrency_disambiguation: The observation contract must distinguish the correlated effect from unrelated writes, either through per-effect records/event identities or through a versioned object history whose transition can be uniquely attributed to this effect. A latest-value-only read with no attribution cannot prove COMMITTED under concurrency.
minimal_observation_contract.finality_for_negative_claims: Absence may become decisive only when the target contract says the relevant observation is complete for the effect's admissible application window and later application of that same admitted effect is impossible without a new mutation. Eventual-consistency delay, asynchronous queues, or an open processing horizon keep absence at UNKNOWN.

COMMITTED: An authoritative observation at version/frontier V contains a uniquely correlated effect record or uniquely attributable transition for logical_effect_id.
The correlation binds the intended request digest d and reports a committed/success outcome, or the target contract makes the uniquely attributable transition itself definitive.
Concurrent unrelated writes do not erase this proof because the witness is effect-correlated rather than inferred from present value alone.
CONFLICT: An authoritative target-side record for the same stable effect/idempotency key binds to an incompatible request digest or a definitive conflicting outcome; or

A complete/final observation proves a mutually exclusive target state for the exact effect namespace after a coverage frontier that includes the entire admissible application horizon for this effect, so later appearance of this effect without a new mutation is ruled out by contract.
A merely different current value, ordinary absence, timeout, or stale read never satisfies CONFLICT by itself.
UNKNOWN: Observation freshness cannot be related to the relevant effect horizon.
The read surface is eventually consistent without a completeness/high-water/finality witness.
Positive state is not uniquely attributable to this effect.
Absence is visible but asynchronous processing or delayed replication could still make the effect appear later.
The target-side record is nonfinal, mutable in an unqualified way, weakly consistent, or not bound to d.

minimal_witness_shapes.per_effect_record: R=(key_or_effect_id, request_digest, outcome, record_version, finality). A matching final-success R is sufficient for COMMITTED; an incompatible digest or final conflicting outcome is sufficient for CONFLICT. Missing R is decisive only if the lookup also supplies a coverage/finality witness proving completeness for this effect horizon.
minimal_witness_shapes.append_only_log_or_index: O=(effect_identity, request_digest, outcome, event_version) plus high-water mark H. A matching event at or below H is sufficient for COMMITTED. Absence below H is not sufficient unless the protocol can establish that every possible application of this effect would necessarily have been indexed by H and the effect's processing window is closed.
minimal_witness_shapes.versioned_object_history: O=(object_version, transition_identity, effect_correlation, value). This can prove COMMITTED only when the transition is uniquely correlated to the intended effect. Present-value equality without transition identity is insufficient under concurrent writers.

bounded_leaf_result.absence_soundness_rule: Negative evidence is sound only when freshness and completeness are both effect-relative. Formally, absence can leave UNKNOWN only if there exists a target-authoritative frontier H such that all applications of the intended effect that can occur from the already-issued submission are guaranteed observable at or before H, the verifier's observation covers through H, and the target contract rules out later application from that same submission. Without all three facts, absence remains UNKNOWN rather than being converted to CONFLICT.
bounded_leaf_result.direct_architecture_contribution: A safe Stage T verifier needs an epistemic contract, not merely a read endpoint: target authority, monotone versioning, effect-relative coverage/finality, and unique effect correlation. These properties let recurring Chat resolve positive evidence under concurrency and sharply delimit the rare case where absence is decisive, while preserving a no-second-mutation crash-window discipline.
falsification_criteria: If V can advance while omitting earlier relevant events with no coverage guarantee, V is not a sufficient freshness witness.
If two distinct effects can share the same correlation fingerprint in the tested namespace, a positive match does not prove COMMITTED.
If a target may asynchronously apply the original submission after the verifier's read, absence at that read cannot prove CONFLICT.
If the target exposes only latest object value and unrelated writers can produce the same value, value equality is not sufficient positive evidence.
If a negative result depends on timeout duration rather than a target-authoritative completeness/finality contract, it remains UNKNOWN.
unresolved_conditions: The next abstract leaf must derive the minimal coupling between the submission/admission horizon and verifier coverage witness needed to make effect-relative negative evidence decidable without assuming a target-specific API.
Concrete target APIs require separate source-qualified checks for consistency, correlation, finality, quota and cost before target-specific claims.
Transport-level duplicate application of the one admitted network send remains outside this leaf unless the target supplies deduplication/idempotency semantics.
